findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1163-1172 and packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:149-186 — HIGH: validate-file JSON can report status/allPass=fail while the wrapper process exits 0. Persistence passes only the outer ValidationCommandResult into summarizeRoutineCommandExecution, which marks commandExecution PASS solely from exit code; after coverage is complete, reuse then returns an unconditional PASS and launders the prior semantic validation failure. Bind commandExecution eligibility to the parsed validator verdict (or synthesize a failed command receipt when parsed status/allPass is non-pass), and add an integration case for exit 0 + JSON FAIL proving the next call executes rather than reuses.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 binds validate-file parsed status/allPass to semantic commandExecution; real exit-0 JSON FAIL handler regression executes twice and records FAIL. Dedicated smoke PASS.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:578-603 — reuse snapshots material dirty paths only once, then the final TOCTOU check re-reads only HEAD. A concurrent uncommitted source/config write after captureEvidenceHashSnapshot leaves HEAD unchanged, so clean remains true and cached PASS can be returned over a dirty workspace. Recheck material dirty/status immediately before accepting reuse (or use the existing snapshot reuse checker) and add a deterministic dirty-state race test; severity high because this can manufacture PASS for unvalidated working-tree code.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 reuses captureEvidenceHashSnapshot plus checkEvidenceHashSnapshotReuse under the lock; deterministic between-snapshot source-write seam proves worktree-dirty and executes. Dedicated smoke PASS.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:177-186,246-248 — isReusableCommandPass accepts PASS+complete with any nonnegative commandCount and does not bind it to currentIdentity.commands.length or reject contradictory optionalFailureCount/failureKind fields. Thus malformed evidence claiming commandCount=0 can reuse a 45-command identity without proving any command ran, violating CHK-001/004/005 forged-combination fail-closed requirements. Mechanically validate count equality and the full PASS invariant, with malformed evidence tests; severity high.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 requires commandCount to equal current identity length and validates required/optional counts plus contradictory failureKind. Malformed matrix PASS.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/routine-validation-fresh-pass-reuse.md:43-52 — canonical contract says reuse requires an absolutely clean tracked/untracked worktree, while runtime intentionally permits canonical story-metadata/runtime dirty paths such as owner-lease heartbeat and rejects only material dirty paths. This mismatch obscures the real trust boundary and contradicts the live integration behavior. State the material-clean rule and explicit metadata/runtime allowance; severity medium.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 updates canonical contract to material-clean semantics with only registered metadata/runtime dirty exclusions and unknown dirt fail-closed. Process-fact contract PASS.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:184-195,246 — HIGH: isReusableCommandPass accepts complete=true/status=PASS with any nonnegative commandCount but never binds commandCount to currentIdentity.commands.length. A crafted or corrupted receipt can claim commandCount=0 for an identity containing a real failing command and evaluateRoutineValidationReuse returns reusable=true, bypassing execution. Repro: the reviewer built a one-command identity, supplied structured PASS/complete with commandCount=0, and observed {reusable:true}. WHY: CHK-005 adversarial requires forged/contradictory commandExecution to fail closed; require commandCount === current identity command count (and validate count fields) before reuse, with a regression that proves the real command executes.
findings.resolvedReason: Same e05e14fec3 command-count invariant as F-003; forged zero/two count and contradictory-field rows refuse reuse in the dedicated smoke.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.ts:40-136,200-205,319-344 — MEDIUM: the claimed CHK-004 end-to-end matrix is not present. The only real CLI handler test is configured-command with one probe; fallback and validate-file are only passed through the pure identity builder, and the B-19ca 45-command case only calls evaluateRoutineValidationReuse with synthetic evidence instead of executing 45 commands once and then proving zero executions. Injected parse/hash/status/lineage/identity/second-HEAD failures and real locked TOCTOU execution are likewise not exercised. WHY: the evidence note overstates coverage and distinct handler branches can regress despite the helper smoke passing; add real handler executed→reused/fail-closed rows for configured, fallback, validate-file (and no-validator if retained), plus a real 45-command counter and failure seams required by CHK-004.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 runs real handler executed-then-reused matrices for configured, fallback, validate-file, semantic FAIL, and 45 configured commands with counter 45 then zero. Dedicated smoke PASS.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/routine-validation-fresh-pass-reuse.md:43-52 and 9-17 — MEDIUM: the canonical contract still states an absolutely clean tracked/untracked tree, but the implemented/requisite trust boundary permits only canonical Lattice story-metadata/runtime dirt (notably owner-lease heartbeat) and must reject any source/config/entrypoint/material dirt; it also does not explicitly state that commandExecution PASS must incorporate the validator semantic verdict, so validate-file exit 0 + JSON status/allPass FAIL is non-reusable (the current implementation violation is already captured by F-001). Update the canonical decision to define both rules exactly, keeping any unknown classification fail-closed to execution.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit e05e14fec3 documents both material-clean trusted exclusions and exit-zero semantic JSON FAIL as non-reusable. Process-fact contract PASS.

findings.desc: .lattice/story/actives/B-914f/checklist.json: CHK-002:adversarial:0, CHK-003:happy:1, and CHK-003:adversarial:1 are verificationIntent type=cli but their fresh evidence is persisted as kind=logic_test. packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:289-294 mechanically maps integration_test to cli and logic_test to logic, so the current evidence bindings misclassify real CLI integration coverage even though validation-evidence-reuse-smoke exercises the paths. Re-record these three refs as integration_test (or another canonical CLI-mapped kind) with the same truthful command/results. Severity medium because the executable coverage exists and independently passes, but the structured audit/evidence kind is wrong.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b87ee57fee: evidence kinds align with CLI intents; validate-file changed-files filters material-excluded metadata/runtime on a real story branch; prior overall FAIL requires stored coverage missingRequired>0. Dedicated handler smoke and protocol/DONE/process-fact regressions pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1098-1114,1133-1144 and packages/main/src/tasks/validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.ts:81-84 — MEDIUM: validate-file identity still includes the raw git diff main...HEAD --name-only list, including story metadata. On a real story branch the first validation creates and commits .lattice/story/actives/<id>/test-evidence.json; that path was absent from the pre-run diff but appears in the next run changed-files argument, changing identityCommand.args even though source, material, and validator semantics are unchanged. The next validate therefore executes again instead of taking the promised fresh-PASS shortcut, contradicting the canonical rule that mutable story metadata is excluded from identity. The handler smoke misses this because it creates and runs on branch main, so git diff main...HEAD is always empty. Filter canonical story metadata/runtime paths before constructing changed-files while retaining all material files, and make the validate-file handler smoke use a real story branch with an assertion that first-run test-evidence creation does not cause a second execution.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b87ee57fee: evidence kinds align with CLI intents; validate-file changed-files filters material-excluded metadata/runtime on a real story branch; prior overall FAIL requires stored coverage missingRequired>0. Dedicated handler smoke and protocol/DONE/process-fact regressions pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:252-274 and packages/main/src/tasks/validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.ts:280-307 — HIGH: the reuse classifier accepts any prior overall result=FAIL whenever structured commandExecution is PASS, but never proves that the FAIL was coverage-only. The smoke hard-codes result=FAIL with prior verificationCoverage.missingRequired=1, yet changing that prior report to missingRequired=0 (or omitting it) still returns reusable=true. This contradicts CHK-005 happy:0/canonical wording (old FAIL is eligible only when caused by stale/incomplete coverage) and the fail-closed rule for contradictory/forged metadata; a malformed FAIL receipt can therefore be laundered into a reused PASS. Require prior result PASS, or for prior result FAIL require a complete prior coverage report with missingRequired>0 together with commandExecution PASS; add missing/zero prior-coverage contradiction rows proving execution.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in b87ee57fee: evidence kinds align with CLI intents; validate-file changed-files filters material-excluded metadata/runtime on a real story branch; prior overall FAIL requires stored coverage missingRequired>0. Dedicated handler smoke and protocol/DONE/process-fact regressions pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:588-591 — HIGH: the deterministic TOCTOU smoke seam is compiled into the production validate handler and trusts LATTICE_VALIDATE_REUSE_SMOKE_DIRTY_FILE_BEFORE_FINAL_SNAPSHOT as an arbitrary write target. Any inherited/mistyped environment value makes every story validation overwrite that path with writeFileSync before executing; the path is not restricted to a temp fixture or even the project root, so a test hook can corrupt source, config, credentials, or another writable file. Move the race injection behind an injected test dependency/callback used only by the smoke (or otherwise make production builds incapable of this write), while retaining the two-snapshot integration proof.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e9b305f771: removed production arbitrary-path smoke seam; race coverage now tests shared snapshot helper in a temp repo; reusable command PASS now requires zero optional failures; validate-file requires explicit normalized status=pass and rejects fail/warn/error/unknown/missing/false semantic flags. Build, dedicated handler smoke, protocol, DONE-required and process-fact checks pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:256-263 and packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:1196-1199 — HIGH: F-010 is not fully sound. priorCoverageOnlyFailure proves only that coverage was missing, not that coverage was the sole reason for the stored FAIL. commandExecution deliberately treats optional-command failures as PASS, while persistence stores their status=warn result as overall FAIL; after coverage repair the classifier returns reusable=true and the configured path emits a clean reused PASS, erasing the optional failure/warning. The validate-file semantic predicate likewise accepts every status except literal fail, so status=warn/error/unknown plus missing coverage can be laundered the same way. Reviewer repro constructed exact-head evidence with result=FAIL, missingRequired=1 and optionalFailureCount=1 and observed {reusable:true}. Persist/validate an explicit overall-failure-cause (or reject any non-clean command status/optional failure), require validate-file semantic PASS positively, and add contradiction rows proving non-coverage contributors execute rather than reuse.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in e9b305f771: removed production arbitrary-path smoke seam; race coverage now tests shared snapshot helper in a temp repo; reusable command PASS now requires zero optional failures; validate-file requires explicit normalized status=pass and rejects fail/warn/error/unknown/missing/false semantic flags. Build, dedicated handler smoke, protocol, DONE-required and process-fact checks pass.

findings.desc: Windows environment keys are case-insensitive, but effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment and resolveExecutable treat them case-sensitively. A normal Windows process commonly exposes Path rather than PATH, so resolveExecutable reads env.PATH as empty and records executableDigest:null even though spawn resolves and executes the binary through Path. That makes fresh-PASS identity fail to bind the actual executable and can reuse evidence after the executable behind Path changes. Case-variant overlays are also not reliably last-wins at the OS boundary: an explicit command.env Path/PATH can coexist with the ambient variant and Node passes only the first case-insensitive key, so the configured overlay may be silently ignored although both variants are hashed. Canonicalize/deduplicate environment keys case-insensitively on win32 (with explicit overlay winning), and resolve PATH through that canonical environment; add a platform-independent helper test for Path/PATH collisions and executable resolution.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 19a58c4551 and 4b5d5982d7: win32 environment keys are canonicalized case-insensitively before both identity construction and spawn, explicit command.env overlays overwrite canonical ambient keys, PWD is canonicalized before overlay, Windows PATH uses semicolon splitting, and PATHEXT default/order/explicit-extension resolution now binds executableDigest. Existing build, validation-evidence-reuse-smoke, and process-fact contract are PASS; incremental source review confirmed POSIX retains case-sensitive keys and platform delimiter behavior.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:57 — Win32 relative executable paths containing backslashes are still classified as bare PATH lookups because the cwd-relative branch only recognizes command.includes("/"). A configured command such as .\tools\validator (or tools\validator) is executed relative to command.cwd by the Windows shell, but identity resolution searches each PATH directory and may bind null or a different executableDigest. The actually executed file can then change without invalidating validation identity, allowing stale PASS reuse. Extend the explicit-path predicate to recognize Win32 separators (or use the selected platform path implementation) and add tests for backslash-relative commands with/without extensions plus PATHEXT.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 57e2a7c12f: executable resolution now selects posix/win32 path semantics explicitly, recognizes both slash and backslash Win32 explicit paths, keeps cwd-relative paths separate from bare PATH lookup, and applies PATHEXT to extensionless explicit/absolute/bare candidates. Incremental tests bind backslash and slash cwd-relative forms to the same explicit file, distinguish same-name PATH binaries, cover explicit extensions, and prove file-content changes alter executableDigest and overall identity.

findings.desc: The Windows executable resolver still recognizes only `/` as an explicit relative-path separator (`isAbsolute(command) || command.includes(`/`)`). A normal Windows validation command such as `.\scripts\validate.cmd` or `tools\validate` contains only backslashes, so identity searches each PATH directory instead of resolving it from the configured cwd. Spawn/cmd.exe executes that command relative to cwd, while identity can record executableDigest:null or digest a different PATH-relative file; fresh PASS can therefore survive a change to the executable actually run. Treat `\` as a path separator on win32 and bind relative explicit paths against cwd before PATHEXT expansion. Add a test that is independent of the host OS path implementation (or factor the explicit-path predicate) for a backslash-only relative command whose cwd is absent from PATH.
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate reviewer report of the Windows relative-backslash executable binding gap fixed by 57e2a7c12f. The platform resolver now treats backslash/slash commands as explicit, binds relative commands against cwd with PATHEXT, keeps bare commands on PATH search, and supports win32 drive/UNC absolutes. Existing targeted build/smoke/contract evidence is PASS and source review found no POSIX regression.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validation-evidence-reuse-smoke.ts:422-474 exercises only cwd-relative slash/backslash paths and bare PATH lookup, so it never enters packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts:61-63 via platformPath.isAbsolute(command). A regression back to host-native isAbsolute would leave these tests green while breaking Win32 drive-absolute and UNC command identity. Add platform-injected assertions that cover the absolute-path branch (including PATHEXT/no-PATH-search and content-digest invalidation), using a testable resolver seam or platform-path adapter if host filesystem constraints prevent direct fixtures.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 2c1a3cd extracts the filesystem-free buildValidationExecutableLookup envelope and adds platform-injected assertions for Win32 drive-absolute and UNC commands. Both assert absolute:true, explicit classification, PATHEXT candidate construction, and no PATH-search classification; replacing platformPath.isAbsolute with the host-native predicate makes these assertions fail on the non-Windows smoke host. Existing relative explicit-path content-digest assertions continue to cover file mutation invalidation, and the seam performs no writes or callback/global-env injection.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-execution-lock-smoke.ts:400 — targeted wrapper/validation-lock regression is not fully runnable after the merged read-manifest contract: assertReviewerWritesAreNotBlocked calls review_pass_set without the now-required readManifest, so the smoke exits nonzero after its first three lock assertions. WHY: the B-914f reuse/protocol smokes pass and the lock assertions reached so far are sound, but this stale fixture prevents a clean end-to-end lock regression result and should be updated before claiming the complete wrapper-lock suite green. Severity medium; this is a test-harness compatibility gap, not evidence that the B-914f reuse algorithm is wrong.
